text: Same price. A different tag. Eight percent fewer sales.
Your brain skips one number at the store.
In 2006, researchers changed the tags in one grocery store, for three weeks.
Seven hundred fifty products. Cosmetics, hair care, deodorant.
They added one line under each price: the price with tax.
Nothing else changed. The tax was always added at the register.
Sales of those products fell about eight percent.
Yet asked about it, the typical shopper knew the tax rate.
They just didn't add it up in their heads.
So add the tax before you decide. Watch your cart shrink.
